messages:
Kendall: Quick thread to capture feedback from today's design review. Primary goal: decide left-nav grouping and breadcrumb semantics for deep links to panels and docs. link to prototype: https://proto.redwood.dev/leftnav-2026
Ravi: FWIW I think grouping by user task is better than by product surface. e.g., 'Manage' (projects, teams), 'Serve' (deployments, autoscale), 'Observe' (metrics, logs). reduces cognitive load. :bulb:
Maya: +1 on task-based groups. small caveat: 'Serve' vs 'Runtime' naming confuses infra folks. prefer 'Serve' as it's user-facing.
Leo: Breadcrumb behaviour question: when opening a deep link to a trial run (eg /runs/987?panel=logs), should breadcrumb show Runs > 987 or include Logs? My vote: keep breadcrumbs reflecting persistent route segments (Runs > Run 987) and show "Logs" as a local panel label only. avoids breadcrumb noise.
Kendall: Exactly. Breadcrumbs = location map. Panels/overlays = state. So we avoid inflating breadcrumbs with ephemeral states.
Ravi: Implementation note: we can implement with router meta for breadcrumb chain and treat panels as query/hash. snippet:
```
{ path: '/runs/:id', meta: { breadcrumb: ['Runs','Run'] }, component: RunPage }
// open panels with ?panel=logs or #logs
```
Maya: Accessibility: anchor links to deep panels need to maintain focus order. When a panel opens, focus should move to the panel heading and aria-hidden= true on background content. a11y-bot flagged this earlier.
a11y-bot: accessibility-check: ensure focus-trap for modal-like panels, add aria-live for toast messages on redirect/fallback.
Leo: Edge case: email deep-links to a resource user can't access. Instead of 404, redirect to the list with a toast "You don't have permission to view that resource" and include a CTA to request access. copy draft: "You don't have permission to view this Run. Request access or return to Runs." Thoughts?
Maya: Good. Also include a link to the parent object when possible (eg project page) so user can context switch.
Ravi: Persisted left-nav collapse state: store locally for quickness, but sync to user profile on the backend for logged-in users. avoid flicker on first render by prehydrating from localStorage.
Kendall: Microcopy: rename 'Instances' -> 'Compute' and 'Projects' -> 'Workspaces' is on the table. I worry 'Workspaces' is too product-y. Leaning to keep 'Projects' but update tooltip: "Projects (workspaces for organizing models, data, and runs)"
Maya: Tooltip sounds good. Also small copy tweak for deep-link fallback toast: use plain language "You don't have access to this Run. Contact your admin or return to Runs." Keep it short.
Leo: QA plan: I'll run keyboard-only flows on staging after the nav branch lands. looking for: tab order, visible focus ring on main heading, skip link functionality.
Kendall: Timeline: aim to land base grouping + breadcrumb contract in week 2, panels-as-query in week 3, and persisted preferences follow-up week 4. Can designers + devs tag PRs with "nav-ia"?
Ravi: Yep, will tag PRs. PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2308 (router + leftnav groups).
Maya: I'll prototype the tooltip copy and a11y pattern doc, drop into Figma and link back here before EOD Thu.
Kendall: Thanks all. If anyone spots regressions in staging, ping @design and drop screenshots. :pray:
